intelligence.title_original: Europe’s rivers are running dry, and the knock-on effects are disastrous | Yiannis Baboulias
intelligence.title_zh: 极端天气风险出现新动态
intelligence.summary_source: Droughts that were once a century now happen every year, and the impact on wildlife, industrial output and culture itself is catastrophic Last week, 186 passengers had to be evacuated from the cruise ship Viking Ullur, after it ran aground on a sandbank in the Danube. Others have been left stranded , unable to move between Vienna and Budapest. Passengers stood on deck, the Habsburg splendour around them out of reach as the river fell to 41cm in Budapest, within 8cm of its 2018 all-time low. Elsewhere on the Hungarian stretch of the river, new record lows were recorded. Farther east in Romania , the Danube recorded its lowest water levels since 1996. A river’s flow is measured in cubic metres per second, and at Baziaș, where the river enters the country, it stood at 1,700m³/s, against a July average of 4,700m³/s. Ferry services were suspended, as were grain barges. Yiannis Baboulias is a Greek writer based in London. His work focuses on European politics, the environment and the far right Continue reading...
